answer: A reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a small time-bound deposit before its attestations count, so spawning many hollow identities costs real capital. Newcomers begin on a low terrace of trust: their votes weigh almost nothing until independent established peers vouch for sustained useful work. Each voucher is capped, and a voucher forfeits part of its own stake if its protege misbehaves, so trust rises like a knoll built gradually from verified ground, while forged swarms stay expensive, slow, and easy to spot.
